# Divider

Figma: [04h. Divider](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-918) · Family: 04 Data Display · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-03

A 1px line that separates content. Horizontal dividers section vertical lists (between KeyValue rows, between Card sections); vertical dividers section horizontal items (in toolbars, breadcrumbs, side-by-side stat groups). Two styles (solid for definitive breaks, dashed for softer separation), three tones (subtle for in-list rhythm, default for section breaks, strong for major divisions). The smallest, most-used component in the system - keep it boring on purpose.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/divider/reference.png`

### Divider

One-pixel line, horizontal or vertical, solid or dashed, in subtle/default/strong tone, that separates rows or sections when whitespace is not enough.

Level: atom · Part of: KeyValue, Table / Cell

Use when:
- Between KeyValue rows in a deal terms panel (Tone=subtle)
- Between sections inside a card (Tone=default)
- Vertical separator between toolbar groups or side-by-side figures
- Dashed before an optional or collapsible details group

Don't use when:
- Separating whole containers: use a card boundary or spacing
- First or last element inside a card: omit it, the card edge separates
- Rows inside ListItem or ActionList: use their built-in divider option

Accessibility: Decorative; hide from assistive tech (role=presentation) unless it marks a real section break.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Orientation | `orientation` | variant | horizontal, vertical | horizontal |
| Variant | `variant` | variant | solid, dashed | solid |
| Tone | `tone` | variant | subtle, default, strong | subtle |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Divider is a 1px line that creates separation between items or sections. It's the smallest component in Syntropy and intentionally narrow in scope - one line, two styles, three tones. The job is to be reliable, predictable, and stay out of the way.

Use Divider when whitespace alone isn't enough to communicate grouping. In a detail panel with rows of KeyValues, subtle dividers between rows make scanning easier. In a Card with several sections, a default divider says "new topic starts here". In a toolbar with grouped buttons, vertical dividers separate function groups.

> **Tip:** When to reach for Divider vs other separators: Divider is a visible 1px line. Use whitespace (margin or itemSpacing) when grouping is implicit. Use a Card boundary when items belong in distinct containers. Use Divider when items are in the same container but you want to visually group them inside it.

### Anatomy

A single 1px line. That's it. The Divider component is a thin frame containing a Rectangle bound to a border color token. For solid variants, the rectangle has a fill. For dashed variants, the rectangle has a 1px stroke with a [4, 4] dash pattern and no fill.

When designers place a Divider instance inside an auto-layout container, they set its Fill container property to make the line span the full width (horizontal) or height (vertical) of the container. The component itself is content-sized at 200×1 (or 1×200) until set to Fill.

A horizontal solid default divider at full container width

### Orientation - horizontal vs vertical

Horizontal dividers (1px tall) separate items stacked vertically. Vertical dividers (1px wide) separate items arranged horizontally. They're structurally identical - the orientation variant just sets which dimension the line spans.

Orientation = horizontal

Spans full container width with 1px height. Use to separate items stacked vertically: KeyValue rows in a detail panel, sections in a Card, menu items in a dropdown, settings rows in a preference list.

Orientation = vertical

Spans full container height with 1px width. Use to separate items arranged horizontally: button groups in a toolbar, segments in a breadcrumb, columns in a side-by-side stat row, action chips in a footer.

### Variant - solid vs dashed

Solid is the default. It says "this is a real, definitive break between items". Dashed signals a softer, more provisional separation - "these items are related but distinct" or "this group can collapse/expand".

Variant = solid

Standard divider for most use cases. Use between KeyValue rows in a detail panel, between Card sections, between menu items. The default choice - reach for solid first.

Variant = dashed

Use sparingly for "softer" separations - between a primary group and an "optional details" group, before a "show more" toggle, or to indicate a divisible/foldable section. Dashed dividers register as less definitive than solid ones.

> **Warning:** Dashed dividers are visually noisier than solid ones - the dash pattern adds rhythm that can compete with the content. Use dashed only when the softness IS the message ("this break is optional"). Default to solid.

### Tone - subtle vs default vs strong

Tone picks the visual weight of the line. Subtle barely registers - use for in-list rhythm where the divider is supporting scannability rather than communicating a real break. Default is the workhorse for section divisions. Strong pulls the eye - reserve for major divisions where the user should notice the shift.

Tone = subtle

Bound to border/subtle. Use between KeyValue rows in a detail panel, between rows in a Table, between menu items. These dividers create scanning rhythm without competing for attention. Most KeyValue lists use Tone=subtle.

Section A - primary content area

Section B - secondary content area

Tone = default

Bound to border/default. Use for section divisions inside a Card, between groups in a Toolbar, between segments in a Breadcrumb. The standard "this is a meaningful break" weight.

Section A - primary content area

Section B - secondary content area

Tone = strong

Bound to border/strong. Use for major page divisions, between primary and secondary content blocks, before a "destructive actions" footer. Reserve for breaks the user should notice without scanning for them.

Section A - primary content area

Section B - secondary content area

### In context - common patterns

Three canonical patterns showing Divider in the real world.

### Pattern 1: Detail panel with KeyValue rows

In a deal detail panel, horizontal subtle dividers create scanning rhythm between KeyValue rows. The dividers register peripherally - the eye scans the labels on the left and values on the right; the dividers just keep the rows from blurring together.

### Pattern 2: Card with section divisions

Inside a Card with multiple sections, default-tone dividers signal "new topic". The weight is enough that the reader notices the shift without being jarred. Use full-bleed dividers (Fill container) for the cleanest look.

Deal summary

Sharia-compliant Sukuk issuance for commercial real estate development.

Issuance details

Target raise 5M ﷼ · 18-month maturity · 12.5% annualized return

Compliance

CMA license SUK-2025-014 · Reviewed by Shariyah Review Bureau

### Pattern 3: Toolbar with grouped actions

Vertical default-tone dividers separate function groups in a toolbar. Each group of related buttons sits between two dividers. The dividers are short (matching the row height) and never bleed beyond the toolbar.

### Content guidance

Divider is the smallest component in Syntropy. The most important guidance is about WHEN to use it - not about Divider itself.

### Prefer whitespace first

- Whitespace (itemSpacing in auto-layout) groups items implicitly without adding visual noise. For most layouts, increasing the gap between items achieves what a Divider would, with less weight.
- Reach for Divider only when the grouping signal needs to be explicit - when items are visually similar and the user needs a hint that one group ends and another begins.

### Prefer the lighter tone

- Default to subtle. Most dividers should barely register - they're for scanning rhythm, not for grabbing attention.
- Step up to default tone only when subtle doesn't register against the background. This happens on bg/elevated where subtle can vanish.
- Use strong tone sparingly - at most one or two per screen. If you find yourself reaching for strong on every divider, you probably want a Card boundary instead.

### Avoid Divider clutter

- Never put a Divider directly inside a Card boundary as the first or last element - the Card edge already provides separation.
- Avoid stacking Dividers with different tones next to each other - pick one tone for a given list/section and stick with it.
- Don't use Divider as decoration. If the divider doesn't serve a grouping purpose, remove it.

### Code examples - Flutter

Reference implementations. Production code lives in lib/design_system/divider/.

### Basic usage

```dart
// Horizontal subtle divider - most common (between KeyValue rows)
const SafqahDivider()

// All defaults: orientation=horizontal, variant=solid, tone=subtle
// Render as a 1px-tall line bound to border/subtle, filling parent width

// Section divider with stronger weight
const SafqahDivider(tone: DividerTone.default_)

// Dashed divider for soft separation (e.g. before "show more" toggle)
const SafqahDivider(variant: DividerVariant.dashed, tone: DividerTone.subtle)

// Vertical divider in a Row (toolbar, breadcrumb)
SizedBox(
  height: 24,
  child: const SafqahDivider(orientation: DividerOrientation.vertical),
)
```

### Composition with KeyValue rows

```dart
// Compose a detail panel: KeyValue rows separated by subtle dividers.
// This is the canonical Syntropy pattern.

class DealDetailPanel extends StatelessWidget {
  final Deal deal;
  const DealDetailPanel({super.key, required this.deal});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final rows = [
      SafqahKeyValue(label: 'Issuance ID', value: deal.id),
      SafqahKeyValue(label: 'Underlying asset', value: deal.underlyingAsset),
      SafqahKeyValue(
        label: 'Profit rate',
        value: '${deal.profitRate}% annualized',
        emphasis: KeyValueEmphasis.strong,
      ),
      SafqahKeyValue(label: 'Maturity period', value: '${deal.maturityMonths} months'),
      SafqahKeyValue(label: 'Sharia advisor', value: deal.shariaAdvisor),
    ];

    return Column(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
      children: [
        for (int i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) ...[
          rows[i],
          if (i < rows.length - 1) const SafqahDivider(),
        ],
      ],
    );
  }
}
```

### Variant resolution

```dart
// File: lib/design_system/divider/safqah_divider.dart
class SafqahDivider extends StatelessWidget {
  final DividerOrientation orientation;
  final DividerVariant variant;
  final DividerTone tone;

  const SafqahDivider({
    super.key,
    this.orientation = DividerOrientation.horizontal,
    this.variant = DividerVariant.solid,
    this.tone = DividerTone.subtle,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final theme = SyntropyTheme.of(context);
    final color = switch (tone) {
      DividerTone.subtle => theme.border.subtle,
      DividerTone.default_ => theme.border.default_,
      DividerTone.strong => theme.border.strong,
    };

    final isHorizontal = orientation == DividerOrientation.horizontal;
    final lineWidget = variant == DividerVariant.solid
        ? Container(
            width: isHorizontal ? double.infinity : 1,
            height: isHorizontal ? 1 : double.infinity,
            color: color,
          )
        : DottedLine(
            direction: isHorizontal ? Axis.horizontal : Axis.vertical,
            dashLength: 4,
            dashGapLength: 4,
            lineThickness: 1,
            dashColor: color,
          );

    return Semantics(
      child: ExcludeSemantics(
        excluding: tone == DividerTone.subtle,  // decorative subtle dividers don't announce
        child: lineWidget,
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Do and Don't

Four pairs of operational guidance.

### Default to subtle tone

- **Do** · Scenario name: Use Tone=subtle for the workhorse case - between rows in a list, between items in a menu, between KeyValue rows in a detail panel. The dividers create rhythm without competing for attention.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't default to default or strong tone. Strong dividers register as "look here" - if every divider screams, none of them are heard.

### Reach for whitespace before Divider

- **Do** · Scenario name: Increase itemSpacing first. If 16-24px gaps already create clear grouping, you don't need a divider. The divider should ADD clarity, not duplicate what whitespace already gives.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't reach for Divider as the default separator. Cluttered layouts with dividers everywhere read as anxious - like the layout doesn't trust the user to follow groupings on their own.

### Use solid first

- **Do** · Scenario name: Solid dividers are the default. They're predictable, calm, and read consistently across themes. Use solid for 95% of divider needs.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't reach for dashed except when you genuinely mean "soft" separation. Dashed signals optionality or foldability - if your section isn't optional or foldable, solid is better.

### Respect Card boundaries

- **Do** · Scenario name: Inside a Card, use Dividers BETWEEN sections. Let the Card's edge handle the outer boundary. Dividers inside a Card stop at the inner padding edges, not at the Card border.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't add a Divider at the very top or bottom of a Card. The Card already has a boundary; an internal divider as the first/last element duplicates the visual signal and looks like an editing mistake.

### Notes from the maintainer

Design decisions, known gaps, and constraints for the next maintainer.

> **Info:** No size variant - all dividers are 1px. A thicker divider would be a Card boundary or a custom visual element. Keeping Divider at one stroke weight prevents the "is this a divider or a banner" ambiguity that creeps in on systems with 1/2/4/8px options.

> **Info:** No inset variant - dividers always span the full width of their container. To create an indented divider (Material-style list separator), wrap the Divider in a frame with left padding. Adding inset as a variant would multiply the variant count (×3 for none/start/both) without serving a real Safqah use case yet. Defer until a real case appears.

> **Info:** Dashed pattern is fixed at 4px on / 4px off. Other dash patterns (6/4, 8/4, dotted) would create style fragmentation across the system. One dash pattern means designers can't accidentally pick a non-canonical one.

> **Tip:** Solid uses a Rectangle FILL bound to the border token. Dashed uses a Rectangle STROKE with the same token and dashPattern [4, 4]. This is a Figma rendering quirk - for solid lines, fill renders cleaner; for dashed, only stroke supports dashPattern. The production Flutter code uses a Container for solid and a DottedLine widget for dashed (see Code Examples).

> **Tip:** Designers must set Fill container when placing the divider inside an auto-layout - the component itself is 200×1 or 1×200 by default. The Library Internals reference frame shows the components at their natural size as a deliberate choice (you can see them in isolation).

> **Info:** No dark mode yet. Divider binds to border/subtle, border/default, border/strong - all three have dark mode definitions in the Semantic collection, so adding dark mode requires no Divider changes once the collection mode is enabled globally.

> **Info:** No RTL variant - a 1px line has no direction. If a future inset variant is added, then RTL will matter (start-side inset flips). Until then, the same component instance works for LTR and RTL surfaces.

> **Warning:** Don't use Divider for vertical dividers between full-height columns on a page - that's a Card boundary or a layout problem. Vertical Divider is for inline contexts (toolbars, breadcrumbs, stat rows) where the line is short (24-32px). A vertical divider running the full height of a page reads as a column boundary, not a divider.
